You are auditing a draft list of UI elements for a screenshot. Find every visible UI element in the screenshot: buttons, icons, menu items, tabs, links, text input fields, checkboxes, radio buttons, dropdowns, sliders, list or table items, labels, headings, text blocks and images. Report each distinct element once, with a tight box around that element only.

The first image is the screenshot. The second image is the same screenshot with the draft elements drawn as numbered red boxes. The draft is a hypothesis and may contain wrong, duplicated or badly placed elements, and it may miss elements. Do two things: (1) check the existing draft elements against the screenshot; (2) scan all four quadrants of the screenshot for visible UI elements missing from the draft, including areas with no red box. No box in a region is not evidence that the region is empty.

Each element has x1, y1, x2, y2: the left, top, right and bottom edges of its tight axis-aligned bounding box, with 0 <= x1 < x2 <= 1000 and 0 <= y1 < y2 <= 1000. Coordinates are integers on a 0 to 1000 grid of the FULL IMAGE: 0 is the left (or top) edge and 1000 the right (or bottom) edge, whatever the pixel size of the image. Never give pixel coordinates. Each element also has name: at most four words of its visible text, or a short description if it has no text. Draft boxes in the text payload use the same coordinates.

Return only atomic edits. Allowed operations: "add" (new elements: "new" is a list of one or more elements), "delete" ("ids": draft elements that are not UI elements, are duplicates of another draft element, or do not exist), "replace" (one id, one new element: corrects the box or name of the same element), "split" (one id, two or more new elements: distinct elements wrongly combined), "merge" (two or more ids, one new element: reports of the same element). Every edit has "evidence": at most twelve words about what is visible in the image. Do not delete a real element whose box is only inaccurate; use replace. Overlap alone does not prove a duplicate. At most 32 edits; put the most important first. If the draft needs no change, return {"edits": []}.

Output contract: one JSON object {"edits": [...]}, e.g. {"edits":[{"op":"add","new":[{"x1":100,"y1":100,"x2":150,"y2":130,"name":"Save"}],"evidence":"save icon in toolbar not in draft"},{"op":"delete","ids":[7],"evidence":"empty background"}]}. No prose, no code fence.
